text:
Max Jones has nothing on the scoresheet after nine games with Edmonton, and it's tempting to stop there. Don't. Fourth-line minutes (about 9 a night) don't give him much room, but the process is closer to fine than the zeros suggest.

Start with his own chances: 0.94 individual expected goals, roughly one goal's worth of looks, without one going in. Then the bigger number. When Jones is on the ice, the Oilers have scored 3.8 fewer goals than the quality of their chances predicts, a big gap for so few minutes. Their share of expected goals at five on five with him out there is 48%, about the same as the team without him.

That fits who he's been. Evolving-Hockey's numbers from last season put his value in defense, with opponents' chances down when he played (93rd percentile, over a small 175 minutes). He's also quick: his top speed is 94th percentile by NHL EDGE. A 28-year-old former first-round pick of the Ducks, he isn't going to drive a line. But if the bounces even out, he looks like a useful depth piece rather than a passenger. We'd give it a few more weeks before judging.
headline: Max Jones is owed a bounce or two
